slides.title: Nephrotic Syndrome: High-Yield Tables
slides.subtitle: MCNS vs FSGS, Nephrotic vs Nephritic & IAP steroid protocols

slides.title: Diagnostic Tetrad & Numbers
points: Nephrotic proteinuria: 3+/4+ dipstick or Spot Up/Uc > 2 mg/mg
24-hour urine protein: > 40 mg/m²/hr (or > 1 g/m²/day)
Hypoalbuminemia: Serum albumin < 3.0 g/dL (IAP 2021)
Hyperlipidemia: Serum cholesterol > 200 mg/dL & edema
slides.highlight: Exam pearl: MC cause in children (1–10 yrs) is Minimal Change Disease (~85%)

slides.title: Nephrotic vs Nephritic Syndrome
slides.subtitle: Nephrotic || Nephritic
points: Massive proteinuria (> 40 mg/m²/hr) || Mild-mod proteinuria + hematuria
Edema (periorbital, generalised) || Hypertension + oliguria + edema
Normal BP & renal function (usually) || Elevated BP, azotemia, ↑ creatinine
Urine: Oval fat bodies, hyaline casts || Urine: RBC casts, dysmorphic RBCs
Serum C3 normal (in MCNS) || Serum C3 low (in PSGN)
slides.highlight: Exam pearl: Gross hematuria & low C3 point toward Nephritic (PSGN), not MCNS

slides.title: MCNS vs FSGS: Key Differences
slides.subtitle: MCNS || FSGS
points: Age: 1–6 years (M > F) || Age: > 6–10 years (adolescents)
LM: Normal glomeruli || LM: Focal segmental sclerosis
EM: Foot process effacement || EM: Effacement + epithelial damage
Proteinuria: Selective (albumin) || Proteinuria: Non-selective
Response: Steroid-sensitive (> 90%) || Response: Often steroid-resistant
slides.highlight: IF microscopy is negative (no immune deposits) in MCNS

slides.title: SSNS vs SRNS & Relapse Terms
slides.subtitle: Term || IAP 2021 Definition
points: Remission || Urine Nil/Trace for 3 consecutive days
Relapse || Urine 3+/4+ for 3 consecutive days
Frequent Relapse (FRNS) || ≥ 2 relapses in 1st 6m or ≥ 4 in 12m
Steroid Dependent (SDNS) || 2 consecutive relapses on/within 14d of stopping
Steroid Resistant (SRNS) || No remission after 6 weeks daily steroids
slides.highlight: IAP 2021 defines SRNS at 6 weeks of daily prednisolone (earlier 4 weeks)

slides.title: Initial Treatment (IAP 2021)
points: Prednisolone 2 mg/kg/d (60 mg/m²) PO daily × 6 weeks (max 60 mg)
Then 1.5 mg/kg (40 mg/m²) PO alternate day × 6 weeks (max 40 mg)
Total initial therapy = 12 weeks; then stop (no routine tapering)
Relapse: 2 mg/kg/d till remission × 3d, then 1.5 mg/kg AD × 4w
Steroid-sparing: Levamisole, MMF, Cyclophosphamide, Tacrolimus
slides.highlight: Avoid live vaccines during high-dose steroids (≥ 2 mg/kg/d for ≥ 14 days)

slides.title: When to Do a Renal Biopsy?
points: Age at onset < 1 year or > 12 years (per IAP 2021)
Steroid resistance (SRNS: no remission after 6 weeks)
Gross hematuria, persistent hypertension, or renal dysfunction
Low serum C3 or features of secondary cause (SLE, HSP)
Secondary SRNS (loss of steroid response during follow-up)
slides.highlight: Exam pearl: Congenital NS (< 3m) is MC due to NPHS1 (Finnish type) gene

slides.title: Complications & Exam Pearls
points: Spontaneous Bacterial Peritonitis (SBP): MC organism = S. pneumoniae
Hypercoagulability: Loss of Antithrombin III → Renal vein thrombosis
Infections: Loss of IgG & Factor B; give Pneumococcal + Varicella vaccines
Hypovolemia: Give 0.9% NS first; 20% Albumin only if severe/refractory
slides.highlight: MC cause of death in children with NS is Infection (SBP / sepsis)

doctor_check: Slide 3: Changed nephrotic proteinuria cut-off from adult '> 3.5g/1.73m²' to pediatric '> 40 mg/m²/hr' for consistency.
Slide 3: Replaced the highlight because morning periorbital edema also occurs in acute glomerulonephritis; highlighted gross hematuria and low C3 instead.
Slide 4: Clarified FSGS LM finding as 'Focal segmental sclerosis' rather than 'Segmental sclerosis (< 50% glom)' since 'focal' denotes < 50% of glomeruli.
Slide 5: Specified FRNS as '≥ 2 relapses in 1st 6m' to match IAP 2021 criteria precisely.
Slide 7: Removed '(congenital)' label from '< 1 year' since 3–12 months is infantile NS, and replaced routine pre-CNI biopsy (dropped in IAP 2021 SSNS guidelines) with 'Secondary SRNS'.
